correctness.rationale: Transform to an invertible parallelepiped image of a cube; strict convexity gives an exact finite-vertex cutoff. Each maximizing corner has strictly positive inward radial slopes by comparison with adjacent cube vertices. A rescaled triangular sphere-section calculation, with a rigorous local Taylor expansion, gives the positive quadratic coefficient and the O(delta^3) remainder. Code checks rational instances and an independently integrated orthogonal benchmark, but the proof does not rely on enumeration.

originality.rationale: The primary 2016 method evaluates full spherical-band overlap numerically and identifies zero-probability cases, but does not provide the four-sign closed critical scale and, crucially, the parameter-uniform quadratic corner-sum onset coefficient for arbitrary invertible triple normals. A 2010 predecessor treats predominantly the two-transit estimate. Neither inspected text reports this complete local asymptotic. Possible earlier convex-geometry analogues remain a historical-priority risk.
residual_risks: An unlocated general convex polytope–sphere contact-area asymptotic may subsume the coefficient by specialization.
General geometric probability algorithms can compute the full probability for fixed systems; the proposed novelty is solely the closed analytic critical/onset description.
The physical selection model omits observational completeness and eccentricity.

value.rationale: The coefficient is a natural, previously non-tabulated local invariant for the onset of simultaneous visibility of three idealized circular planetary transits. The full generality over triple orbital geometries and arbitrary relative widths makes this useful for near-critical sensitivity and small-probability interpretation, not an arbitrary numerical parameter slice.
